response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T1","text":"Okay, thanks everyone for joining. This is our kickoff for the CCTNS project, the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems under the e-governance Mission Mode Project. Let's get started."},{"id":"M1:T2","text":"Sure, so a bit of background. With CCTNS V1.0 the main idea behind the functional design is to focus on the critical functionality that actually gives value to police personnel at the cutting edge, so we can improve outcomes in \"Investigation of Crime\" and \"Detection of Criminals\". It's really aimed at delivering value to IOs, records room staff and citizens, all within the broad crime investigation area. Based on that, we've identified nine different function blocks and worked out the detailed functionality for each one."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Great. Let's start with the help module. What do you need there?"},{"id":"M1:T4","text":"For help, the solution should have detailed context-sensitive help material covering all the possible actions and scenarios, on every user interface in the application."},{"id":"M1:T5","text":"Anything else on the help module?"},{"id":"M1:T6","text":"No, that's it."},{"id":"M1:T7","text":"Okay, moving on to general needs. What should we capture there?"},{"id":"M1:T8","text":"So first, if the user chooses to, the solution should send them alerts, email or SMS for example, whenever any action has been taken on the alert. And second, users should be able to track a defect or enhancement request they've submitted."},{"id":"M1:T9","text":"So just to confirm, a user who submits a defect or an enhancement request can track it afterwards?"},{"id":"M1:T10","text":"Yes, exactly."},{"id":"M1:T11","text":"And the help-desk user should be able to view reports on those submitted defects or enhancement requests, broken down category-wise, status-wise and age-wise."},{"id":"M1:T12","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T13","text":"Anything else under general needs?"},{"id":"M1:T14","text":"Nothing from me."},{"id":"M1:T15","text":"Alright, let's talk about the audit module."},{"id":"M1:T16","text":"Right, so an audit trail is a record of actions taken either by the user or by system triggers. That covers actions by users or Administrators, and also actions the system starts automatically because of system parameters. The System has to keep an unalterable audit trail that automatically captures and stores information about all the actions, create, read, update, delete, taken on the critical entities like case, suspect, property and so on; the user initiating and or carrying out the action; the date and time of the event; and administrative parameters. By unalterable we mean no user can modify the audit trail data in any way or delete it. It may be subject to re-department and copied to removable media if required, as long as the contents stay unchanged. And once the audit trail functionality is activated, the System has to track events without any manual intervention and store information about them in the audit trail."},{"id":"M1:T17","text":"Also, the System must keep the audit trail for as long as it's required, and that's at least the life of the case it refers to."},{"id":"M1:T18","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T19","text":"From the technical side, audit trail data needs to be available for inspection on request, so a specific event can be identified and all the related data made accessible. And authorised external personnel with little or no familiarity with the system should be able to do that."},{"id":"M1:T20","text":"Yes, and the System must be able to export audit trails for specified cases, without affecting the audit trail the System stores. External auditors can use that if they want to examine or analyse system activity. And at a minimum, it should provide reports on actions on cases organised by case, by user, and in chronological sequence."}]}
